about: spec-v1974: per-state adoption of the IECC, drafted one state at a time from the state's own statute or rule, with ICC's adoption map as the cross-check only. Each row also names its code family (a state on the UPC or UMC adopts no IPC or IMC edition). All 51 drafted 2026-10-20 from the state's own rule where found, with ICC's April 2026 chart and the DOE state portal as cross-checks; residential and commercial editions are listed separately. Unsigned rows show labeled not verified; a row whose sources conflict shows no edition.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.pending: Act 2024-443 moves the residential energy code to the Home Builders Licensure Board; builders must follow its code from 2027-01-01.
AL.scope: Enforced by local jurisdictions that enforce codes. Commercial may comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2013 instead.
AL.citation: Ala. Admin. Code r. 305-2-4-.10 (residential, 2015 IECC as modified) and r. 305-2-4-.08 (commercial), Energy and Residential Codes Board
AL.draft_note: Read rule 305-2-4-.10: 'The 2015 International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) as modified', (2) 'this code shall become effective on October 1, 2016' (amended eff 2017-10-05). Read rule 305-2-4-.08: 'Either the 2015 International Energy Conservation Code or the ANSI/ASHRAE/IES Standard 90.1-2013 shall be implemented and enforced for commercial buildings', effective 2016-01-01. Read HB198 enrolled (2024; Act 2024-443 per a Justia note on 34-14A-12.1, passed 2024-05-09, effective 2024-10-01): repeals 41-23-80 et seq., gives the Home Builders Licensure Board sole authority over an 'Alabama Residential Energy Code', enforced by local jurisdictions that have adopted energy code provisions, and moves the commercial code to a Commercial Energy Code division. No HBLB residential energy code rule found, and the ADECA rules are still served by the Administrative Code, so they are recorded as in force; signer: confirm whether HBLB has replaced r. 305-2-4-.10. DOE lists both as mandatory statewide (res 2015 IECC eff 2016-10-01, com 90.1-2013 eff 2016-01-01). Status 'statewide-amended' follows DOE; the IRC row says 'limited' because of pre-2010 local codes, which may apply here too.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.scope: Only state-financed residential buildings and state-assisted community buildings (AHFC BEES); no general statewide energy code.
AK.citation: 15 AAC 155.010-.020 (Building Energy Efficiency Standard: 2018 IECC with Alaska amendments), Alaska Housing Finance Corporation
AK.draft_note: Read 15 AAC 155.010 on akleg.gov: 'The International Energy Conservation Code of 2018, with Alaska-specific amendments dated November 28, 2018 ... shall constitute the building energy efficiency standards for Alaska. The standards apply to buildings whose construction began on or after January 1, 2019', residential and commercial buildings subject to AS 46.11.040. 155.020: applies to residential buildings receiving state financial assistance and community-owned buildings built with state assistance; communities may be exempted on fuel-cost grounds. Effective date is the construction-start date in the rule; the register date was not read. 13 AAC 50.020 (state fire marshal) adopts the IBC, not the IECC. DOE lists Home Rule, voluntary. Other buildings: local codes (e.g. Anchorage).

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.scope: No statewide energy code; cities and counties adopt their own IECC edition, or none.
AZ.citation: No state adoption: counties adopt building codes under A.R.S. 11-861; cities by reference under A.R.S. 9-802
AZ.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. The IBC row read A.R.S. 11-861 and 9-802 on azleg.gov (local adoption authority). DOE state page: residential and commercial 'Home Rule', enforcement 'Jurisdictional'. No state energy code rule found. Signer: confirm no state rule.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.pending: 2021 IECC adoption by the Arkansas Energy Office reported in progress since 2023; no proposed or final rule found.
AR.scope: Every county or city that issues building permits must adopt it. Commercial may comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2007.
AR.citation: Ark. Code R. 168.00.14-001 (Arkansas Energy Code: 2009 IECC with Arkansas amendments), Arkansas Energy Office; Ark. Code 15-10-205
AR.draft_note: Read the rule text (Cornell LII copy, dated 9/12/2014): 'Arkansas adopts the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC), 2009 Edition', amendments take precedence; 'The effective date for this Code shall be is 1/1/2015'; all counties, cities or municipalities that issue building permits must adopt it (Ark. Code 15-10-205(b)(3)(B)); commercial alternative path ASHRAE 90.1-2007 via IECC Ch. 5. A March 2021 draft of 2021 amendments (ADEQ site) aimed at 2024-01-01 but no final rule found; BCAP said 2021 adoption anticipated 2025. DOE agrees (2009 IECC, 01/01/2015). Not checked: whether the 2021 Arkansas Fire Prevention Code Vol. III (2021 IRC) keeps IRC Ch. 11 or defers to this code.

CA.name: California
CA.scope: California Energy Code (Title 24, Part 6, 2025 Standards), the state's own code, not based on the IECC; residential and nonresidential.
CA.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 24, pt. 6 (2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards), California Energy Commission
CA.draft_note: Read the CEC 2025 standards page: 'Buildings whose permit applications are applied for on or after January 1, 2026, must comply with the 2025 Energy Code', covering residential, nonresidential and multifamily. The California Energy Code is written by the CEC and is not an amended IECC, so family 'other' with no IECC edition. DOE lists '2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards' eff 01/01/2026 (equivalent 2024 IECC / 90.1-2022). Cities may adopt stricter local energy ordinances approved by the CEC.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.scope: No statewide code; local codes updated 2023-07-01 to 2026-06-30 must meet the 2021 IECC, later ones the model low energy and carbon code.
CO.citation: No state adoption: C.R.S. 31-15-602(3.5) and 30-28-211 set the minimum energy code a city or county must adopt when it updates codes
CO.draft_note: Read C.R.S. 31-15-602 (colorado.public.law copy): (3.5)(a) a municipality that updates a building code on or after 2023-07-01 and before 2026-07-01 must adopt an energy code at least equal to the 2021 IECC plus the model electric-ready and solar-ready code; (3.5)(b) updates on or after 2026-07-01 must meet the model low energy and carbon code (per the Colorado Energy Office, based on the 2024 IECC; CEO page returned 403, search summary only); (3.5)(e) allows compliance by 2030-06-30 in some cases. County twin 30-28-211 not read beyond its findings. So the edition varies by jurisdiction and when it last updated; no state edition is in force for a building. citation_primary true because the statute read is the state's own text; signer may prefer false as for other absences. State buildings (OSA/DFPC) not checked. DOE: Home Rule, Jurisdictional.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.pending: 2026 State Building Code (2024 IECC) awaits Legislative Regulation Review Committee approval; July 1, 2026 date delayed, no new date.
CT.scope: Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2019.
CT.citation: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code (2021 IECC as amended), Office of the State Building Inspector, C.G.S. 29-252
CT.draft_note: Read DAS regulations page: the 2022 Connecticut State Building Code lists the '2021 International Energy Conservation Code' among adopted model codes and 'applies to projects with permit applications filed from October 1, 2022'. Read DAS adoption-process page: the 2024 IECC is listed for the 2026 code, expected 2026-07-01 but delayed awaiting LRRC approval, no date. A March 2026 State Codes and Standards Committee agenda (search summary only) says the proposed 2026 code was withdrawn 2026-02-23; not resolved. ASHRAE 90.1-2019 path is per DOE (2021 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2019, eff 10/01/2022), not read in the CT amendments.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.scope: State minimum; counties and cities must meet it within 12 months of adoption. Commercial may comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2022.
DE.citation: 7 Del. Admin. Code 2101 (2024 IECC; 90.1-2022 for commercial), DNREC Secretary's Order 2026-CCE-0002; 16 Del. C. 7602
DE.draft_note: Read Secretary's Order No. 2026-CCE-0002: 'Date of Issuance: March 10, 2026 / Effective Date of the Amendment: April 11, 2026'; adopts by reference the 2024 IECC for residential and the 2024 IECC / ASHRAE 90.1-2022 for commercial and high-rise residential, plus amended Appendix RE (EV) and CB (solar-ready); ZNE-capable amendments dropped. Prior code: 2018 IECC / 90.1-2016 adopted June 2020. Read 16 Del. C. 7602(a): county and municipal codes 'shall meet the most recent version ... within 12 months of adoption by the Delaware Energy Office', so some local codes may still enforce the 2018 IECC until about 2027-04-11. DOE agrees (2024 IECC, eff 04/11/2026). ICC chart (18, 90.1-2016) is chart lag.

FL.name: Florida
FL.pending: 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code, incl. Energy Conservation, proposed 2026-09-23; no final notice or date yet.
FL.scope: Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2019.
FL.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61G20-1.001 (Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023), Energy Conservation), Florida Building Commission
FL.draft_note: Read flrules page for 61G20-1.001: 8th Edition (2023) FBC adopted (Energy volume referenced in 2025 notices), latest final eff 2026-03-18; proposed notice 2026-09-23 adopts the 9th Edition (2026). Effective 2023-12-31 per the IRC/IBC rows' reading of the notice history. 2021 IECC base: Florida Building Commission DOE certification letters (search summary only) say the 8th Edition residential provisions meet or exceed the 2021 IECC and commercial provisions meet ASHRAE 90.1-2019; ICC product listing says based on 2021 IECC. DOE agrees (2021 IECC / 90.1-2019, eff 12/31/2023). Signer: confirm the base edition in the FBC-EC preface.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.pending: DCA Energy Code Task Force reviewing the 2024 IECC (recommendation due July 2026); no DCA Board adoption found.
GA.scope: Mandatory state minimum code, enforced by local governments that choose to. Commercial may comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2013.
GA.citation: O.C.G.A. 8-2-23; DCA Georgia State Minimum Standard Energy Code: 2015 IECC with Georgia Supplements and Amendments
GA.draft_note: Read DCA 'Georgia State Supplements and Amendments to the IECC (2015 Edition), Revised January 1, 2023': the 2015 IECC with these supplements 'shall constitute the official Georgia State Minimum Standard Energy Code'; COMcheck path allows IECC 2015 or ASHRAE 90.1-2013. Read DCA memo of 2025-12-01: the 2024 IRC, IBC, IPC, IMC, IFGC etc. took effect 2026-01-01 but the energy code is not on the list. Effective date 2020-01-01 (2015 IECC base) is from DOE and a search summary of DCA's 'Revised January 1, 2020' edition; signer confirm. Task force status from Southface page (search summary). HBA of Georgia letter (2025-10-07) asked DCA to pause 2024 IECC adoption.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.pending: SBCC adopted the 2021 IECC with amendments (Dec 2022); not in HAR and counties still enforce 2018; SBCC updates suspended by proclamation.
HI.scope: Counties adopt and amend the state energy code; if one misses the deadline it applies as the interim county code.
HI.citation: Haw. Admin. R. tit. 3, State Energy Conservation Code (amendments to the 2018 IECC), eff. Dec 15, 2020; HRS 107-24, 107-28
HI.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: Cornell LII HAR copy is 'Amendments to the 2018 ICC International Energy Conservation Code', 'Effective Date: December 15, 2020'. Read a DAGS/SBCC memo (ags.hawaii.gov, Jan 2023) 'Adopting the 2021 IECC and Amendments' 'as adopted by the State Building Code Council in accordance with HRS 107-24'; counties must adopt it or it becomes the interim county energy code under HRS 107-28(b) (adoption date 2022-12-15 from search summaries; no HAR version found). The State Energy Office page (search summary) says as of 2024 all counties enforce the 2018 IECC with county amendments; DOE also lists 2018 IECC eff 12/15/2020, jurisdictional. Same 2018-vs-2021 question as the IRC and IBC rows. Signer: decide.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.pending: Building Code Board proposed the 2024 I-codes (2025-08-11 minutes, per IRC/IBC rows); June 2026 rule text still adopts the 2018 IECC.
ID.scope: Enforced where a city or county runs a permit program (Idaho Code 39-4116) and by the Division for public buildings.
ID.citation: IDAPA 24.39.30.600.05-.06 (IECC Commercial and Residential Provisions, 2018 Edition, amended)
ID.draft_note: Read the current IDAPA 24.39.30 PDF (created 2026-06-12): 600.05 adopts the 2018 IECC Commercial Provisions (adds C101.5.2 industrial-equipment exemption, economizer amendment) and 600.06 the 2018 IECC Residential Provisions (amends R202, replaces Table R402.1.2 rows for CZ 5/6), both stamped (7-1-24). The 2021-01-01 effective date is taken from the IRC/IBC rows for the same 2020 rule package (Division notice and city notices, secondary). 'limited' to match the IRC/IBC rows; signer may prefer 'statewide-amended'. The 2024 proposal is from the IRC/IBC rows; I did not see whether it includes the IECC.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.scope: Residential is a minimum and maximum; towns may opt into the Illinois Stretch Energy Code. Applies statewide to new permits.
IL.citation: 71 Ill. Adm. Code 600.300, 600.400 (Illinois Energy Conservation Code; 2024 IECC with Appendix A amendments)
IL.draft_note: Read 71 Ill. Adm. Code 600.300 (privately funded commercial) and 600.400 (residential) on the ILGA public file repository (ftp.ilga.gov; www.ilga.gov blocks scripts): both incorporate the 2024 IECC (published May 2024), amended at 49 Ill. Reg. 15562, effective 2025-11-30. Read the Capital Development Board page: 'The 2024 edition of the IECC as amended went into effect on 11/30/25' for both. 600.110 (last amended eff. 2025-01-01) still names the 2021 code effective 2024-01-01; it was not updated with the 2024 rule, which I read as a stale purpose clause, not a conflict. 600.110(d)(2): the code applies to any new building for which a municipality or county receives a permit application. Chicago enforces its own energy code under the Act's home-rule provisions (not read here). ICC's April 2026 chart (24/24) agrees.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.scope: Residential energy is Ch. 11 of the 2020 Indiana Residential Code (2018 IRC). Commercial is ASHRAE 90.1-2007 only (675 IAC 19-4).
IN.citation: 675 IAC 14-4.4 (2020 Indiana Residential Code, 2018 IRC incl. Ch. 11); 675 IAC 19-4 (ASHRAE 90.1-2007)
IN.draft_note: Read the IDHS FPBSC rules page: 675 IAC 14-4.4, 2020 Indiana Residential Code, adopts the 2018 IRC, effective 2019-12-26; 675 IAC 19-4, 2010 Indiana Energy Conservation Code, adopts ANSI/ASHRAE 90.1-2007, effective 2010-05-06, both 'Currently in Effect'. Residential energy rules are IRC Chapter 11 (the IECC residential provisions) as amended by Indiana; I did not read Indiana's Chapter 11 amendments, which may keep some older values, so the signer should check how far they depart from the 2018 IECC. No IECC commercial edition is adopted, so commercial is omitted. ICC's chart (18 / 90.1-2007) agrees.
IN.icc_2026_10_20: Master I-Code chart (April 2026): IECC-R 18, IECC-C 90.1-2007 min.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.scope: Energy rules apply statewide to new construction; renovation of 1- and 2-family homes is not covered.
IA.citation: 481 IAC 301.24 and 301.25(103A) (State Building Code energy conservation; IECC 2012 residential and commercial, amended)
IA.draft_note: Read 481 IAC ch. 301 (IAC 9/30/26), Part 3: 301.24 adopts the 2012 IECC Residential Provisions (three or fewer stories, statewide) and 301.25 the 2012 IECC Commercial Provisions, both amended [ARC 9474C eff. 9/10/25; 301.24 also ARC 0412D eff. 8/12/26, which changed an amendment, not the edition]. 301.23(2): Part 3 applies throughout the state. The 2012 edition first took effect 2014-03-12 per ARC 1301C (read on rules.iowa.gov; transition: projects begun 2014-01-01 to 2014-05-31 could use either edition). Unlike the IBC/IRC (2024, limited), the energy code is still 2012 and statewide. ICC's chart (12/12) agrees.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.scope: Statute names the 2006 IECC for new commercial/industrial buildings, but no state agency enforces it; cities and counties adopt their own.
KS.citation: K.S.A. 66-1227 (IECC 2006 adopted as the applicable energy efficiency standard for new commercial and industrial structures)
KS.draft_note: Read K.S.A. 66-1227 on ksrevisor.gov: (a) adopts the IECC 2006 as the applicable standard for new commercial and industrial structures; (b) the KCC has no authority to adopt or enforce energy standards; (c) cities and counties may adopt their own. Read 2007 Session Laws ch. 100 (HB 2036), which changed IECC 2003 to 2006; history line says effective July 1 (2007). No residential code: 66-1228 only requires builders to disclose a new home's energy features. 2025 SB 170 (would amend 66-1227) had a Feb 2025 hearing; no enactment seen. 'limited' because the statute names an edition with no enforcing agency; the signer may prefer 'local' with editions []. DOE energycodes.gov lists Kansas as 'Home Rule'.
KS.icc_2026_10_20: Master I-Code chart (April 2026): IECC-R X, IECC-C X (local adoptions only).

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.pending: DHBC task forces are reviewing newer I-code editions (December 2025 notice, secondary); no rule filed.
KY.scope: R-2/R-3/R-4 buildings of 3 stories or less under the KBC use Ch. 4 of the 2009 IECC.
KY.draft_note: Read the DHBC 2018 Kentucky Building Code, 4th ed. (Feb 2024), incorporated by 815 KAR 7:120: 1301.1.1 requires the 2012 IECC, with an exception sending R-2/R-3/R-4 of 3 stories or less to 2009 IECC Ch. 4. Read the 2018 Kentucky Residential Code (DHBC, July 2020 text): N1101.1 regulates energy efficiency per the 2009 IECC. 815 KAR 7:125 now incorporates the KRC Third Edition (Aug 2024), which I did not read; I assume it keeps N1101. DHBC 'Find Currently Enforced Code' lists the 2012 IECC (commercial only) and 2009 IECC (residential only). Dates are when the current KBC/KRC packages took effect (from the IBC/IRC rows); earlier KBC/KRC editions may already have named these IECC editions, so the original dates may be earlier.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.pending: 2024 I-code cycle proposed (La. Register 2026-08-20) for 2027-01-01; I did not confirm that the IECC is included.
LA.scope: Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2019 (IECC C401.2), which the state energy office lists for commercial.
LA.citation: LAC 17:I.117 (Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code; IECC 2021 Edition, amended)
LA.draft_note: Read LAC 17 Part I (doa.la.gov .docx): §117 adopts the IECC 2021 Edition and referenced standards, with Louisiana amendments (C301.2 warm-humid counties, C402.1.3 slab insulation, C402.5.9 vestibules). Read the LUCCC code information sheet (revised 2026-08-06): 'On 07/01/2023, the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) became effective', 2021 edition. DENR Office of Energy (search snippet, secondary): ASHRAE 90.1-2019 for commercial and the 2021 IECC for low-rise residential since 2023-07-01, which matches the IECC's ASHRAE path, not a conflict. The 2024 proposal is from the IRC/IBC rows.

ME.name: Maine
ME.scope: MUBEC must be enforced in towns of 4,000+, optional below. Towns may opt into the MUBEC Stretch Code (2021 IECC appendices).
ME.citation: 16-642 C.M.R. ch. 6 (MUBEC Energy Code; 2021 IECC, commercial and residential, amended)
ME.draft_note: maine.gov returns 403 to scripts, so I read Wayback copies. 16-642 ch. 6 (642C006_0.pdf, archived 2026-02-12): 'IECC' means the 2021 IECC; Sections 5 and 6 amend its commercial and residential provisions; Appendix NA is the opt-in Stretch Code; effective 90 days after Commissioner approval; last amended March 4, 2025 (filing 2025-047). The State Fire Marshal's 'MUBEC Standards and Amendments' sheet (archived 2025-09-16) says 'Effective beginning April 7, 2025' and lists the 2021 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2019. The prior ch. 6 adopted the 2015 IECC effective 2021-07-01. Signer: 2025-04-07 vs. the 2025-03-04 filing date, as for the IRC/IBC rows.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.pending: 2024 IECC proposed for COMAR 09.12.51 (Md. Register 2026-06-26, comments closed 2026-07-27); no final rule seen.
MD.scope: Statewide minimum (MBPS); counties and cities have 12 months to enforce a state update and may add local amendments.
MD.citation: COMAR 09.12.51.04 (Maryland Building Performance Standards; 2021 IECC with State modifications)
MD.draft_note: Read COMAR 09.12.51.04 on regs.maryland.gov: A(3) incorporates the 2021 IECC; D modifies it (C101 note on PUA 7-401 to 7-408; C405.2.5 hotel guest-room controls). The 2023-05-29 effective date and 12-month local window come from the IRC/IBC rows (DOL COMAR PDF, .06B). The 2024 proposal is from those rows (search results); I did not read the Md. Register notice. The edition at a given address can lag up to 12 months after a state update.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.scope: Base code statewide; most towns have opted into the DOER Stretch or Specialized code (225 CMR 22/23), also 2021 IECC-based.
MA.citation: 780 CMR ch. 11R and ch. 13 (10th edition base energy code; 2021 IECC with MA amendments)
MA.draft_note: mass.gov blocks scripts; read a Wayback copy (2025-02-12) of DOER's '2024/2025 Massachusetts Building Energy Codes' page: 'The Base Code is IECC 2021 with MA amendments: 780 CMR Chapter 11R (residential) and 780 CMR Chapter 13 (commercial)'; the opt-in Stretch Code is 225 CMR 22/23 and the opt-in Specialized Code adds Appendix RC/CC. Effective date is the 10th edition's 2024-10-11 start (from the IBC/IRC rows); the 9th edition could be used until 2025-06-30. I did not read 780 CMR 11R/13 themselves. DOER's 2025 amendments to 225 CMR 23 also reference ASHRAE 90.1-2019 (title, search result).

MI.name: Michigan
MI.pending: 2021 residential energy rules (due 2025-08-29) paused by a 2025-07-07 Court of Claims order, HBA of Michigan v. LARA.
MI.scope: Residential energy is Michigan Residential Code Ch. 11 (2015 IECC base). Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2019.
MI.citation: 2015 Michigan Residential Code Ch. 11; 2021 Michigan Commercial Energy Code (LARA BCC, Stille-DeRossett-Hale Act)
MI.draft_note: LARA Code Books page read 2026-10-20 (curl): '2021 Michigan Commercial Energy Code - Current Code - Effective April 22, 2025'; also lists '2015 Michigan Energy Code - Effective September 20, 2017' with 'Residential requirements are contained in the Michigan Residential Code' (the IRC row read '2015 MRC ... Effective February 8, 2016'). ASHRAE 90.1-2019 alternative from secondary sources (ICC-NTA, Bay City), not seen on LARA's page. Residential 2021 rules stayed by the HBA v. LARA order; no ruling found. R 408 rule numbers not read.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.pending: DLI request for comments 2026-02-02 on chapter 1322 update to 2024 IRC Ch. 11; draft, hearing, dates 'to be determined'.
MN.scope: Commercial (and residential 4+ stories) is ASHRAE 90.1-2019 only, Minn. R. ch. 1323, effective 2024-01-05; no IECC commercial option.
MN.citation: Minn. R. 1322.0010 (2012 IECC residential Ch. 2-5 RE, as amended); Minn. R. 1323.0010 (ASHRAE 90.1-2019)
MN.draft_note: 1322.0010 read: incorporates Ch. 2(RE)-5(RE) of the 2012 IECC (history 33 SR 1480; 39 SR 232). DLI 2020 residential energy fact sheet read: 'effective Feb. 14, 2015'. 1323.0010 read: ASHRAE 90.1-2019 (history to 47 SR 983); DLI 2024 commercial fact sheet read: 'effective Jan. 5, 2024'. ICC's IECC-C 'X' reflects the ASHRAE-only commercial code. Pending docket from search summary of DLI page, not read directly. Same local-enforcement caveat as the IRC row (326B.121) not re-checked for the energy code.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.scope: Council codes are local minimum codes; MDA rule adopts ASHRAE 90.1-2016 for non-low-rise buildings (reach unconfirmed).
MS.citation: No mandatory statewide IECC; Miss. Admin. Code 6-3-5.2 (MDA adopts ASHRAE 90.1-2016; Miss. Code 57-39-21)
MS.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: ICC's April 2026 chart lists IECC-R 18 and IECC-C '18 & 90.1-2010' as state adoptions; DOE's state profile says 'None Statewide' for both. MDA rule 6-3-5.2 (Cornell LII copy, adopted 2018-04-15, amended 2024-03-04) adopts ASHRAE 90.1-2016 for buildings except low-rise residential; which buildings it binds (state-owned only, or all commercial) was not read in 57-39-21. Building Codes Council list not reached (same as IRC/IBC rows); AWC says the Council adopted the 2018 I-codes incl. IECC in Dec 2019.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.scope: No statewide energy code; cities and counties adopt their own IECC edition.
MO.citation: No state adoption: Missouri has no statewide energy code; counties and cities adopt codes by ordinance
MO.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite; no Missouri statute was read. ICC's chart marks IECC-R and IECC-C X (local only), consistent with the IRC/IBC rows. State-owned-building energy standards (FMDC) not looked up.
MO.icc_2026_10_20: Chart (April 2026): IECC-R X, IECC-C X (local adoption only).

MT.name: Montana
MT.scope: Energy provisions apply to small homes too, by builder self-certification, where the rest of the state code does not (MCA 50-60-102).
MT.citation: Admin. R. Mont. 24.301.161 (IECC as amended by ARM Title 24, Ch. 301); MCA 50-60-102
MT.draft_note: DLI Current Codes page read 2026-10-20: 'International Energy Code, 2024 Edition- Effective: Septemeber 26, 2026', amended by ARM Title 24 Ch. 301. Justia copy of ARM 24.301.161 (through Sept 2024) still shows the 2021 IECC; the 2024 rule text and MAR notice were not read. Prior 2021 IECC date (2022-06-11) carried from the IRC row, not re-read. Self-certification note from the IRC row's reading of MCA 50-60-102. Chart lag: ICC's April chart predates the change.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.scope: Local energy codes allowed if equivalent (81-1618). Commercial may comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2016 via IECC C401.2.
NE.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1609 (Nebraska Energy Code = 2018 IECC); 81-1614 (construction starting on/after July 1, 2020)
NE.draft_note: 81-1609 read: 'Nebraska Energy Code means the 2018 International Energy Conservation Code' (source through LB405 2019; LB317 2025). 81-1614 read: applies to new buildings, renovations and additions on which construction starts on or after July 1, 2020. 81-1618: county/city/village may adopt an equivalent local code. Exemptions in 81-1615 (unheated, federal, manufactured/modular, historic). The ASHRAE option is the IECC's own C401.2 path; statute names no ASHRAE edition.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.scope: State minimum; each local government with building-code authority must incorporate and enforce it and may be stricter (NRS 701.220(4)).
NV.citation: NRS 701.220; NAC 701.185 (Governor's Office of Energy adopts current IECC, R153-17); 2024 IECC as amended 2025-03-12
NV.draft_note: GOE status page read: 2024 IECC adopted 'effective August 18, 2024' under NAC 701.185 (R153-17); GOE Notice of Adoption PDF read (objections due 2024-11-15; hearings only if compelling evidence). GOE NAC 701 page: amendments to the 2024 IECC 'effective March 12, 2025' (Appendix A, not read). NRS 701.220 read (summary): triennial IECC adoption; local governments must incorporate and enforce. Local adoption may lag (city/county editions not checked); 2024-08-18 is GOE's adoption date, not a local enforcement date.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.scope: Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2016 (IECC C401.2). The 2026 I-code update kept the IECC at 2018.
NH.citation: RSA 155-A:1, IV (state building code: International Energy Conservation Code 2018, with board amendments)
NH.draft_note: RSA 155-A:1, IV read 2026-10-20 (source line ends 2026 ch. 318:3, eff. July 1, 2026): 'the International Energy Conservation Code 2018'. HB1180 (2026, IECC 2024) got an Inexpedient to Legislate committee report 2026-02-18; HB96 (2025, IECC 2021) not enacted per the current text. Effective date uncertain: BCRB summary (HB1681-2022) says 'Effective July 1, 2022'; DOE profile says 2023-01-01; EnergyBot 2022-09-15. Fire Marshal codes page blocked (403).

NJ.name: New Jersey

NJ.draft_note: Adoption notice 58 N.J.R. 8(2) read: amends 5:23-3.18; adopted 2026-07-15, effective August 17, 2026; responses confirm 'the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code and ASHRAE 90.1-2022', amended. The 3.18 edition lines themselves were not shown in the adopted text. Six-month grace period (to ~2027-02-17) lets prior IECC/2021 + 90.1-2019 (adopted 2022-09-06, enforced 2023-03-06) be used. DCA Bulletin 22-1 (search summary): IECC commercial portion deleted. Chart lag: ICC's April chart predates the change.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.scope: Applies where CID has jurisdiction; a few home-rule jurisdictions adopt their own codes.

NM.draft_note: 14.7.6 and 14.7.9 NMAC read (srca.nm.gov): each 'adopts by reference the 2021 international energy conservation code (IECC), as amended'; 'EFFECTIVE DATE: January 30, 2024'; either the prior 2018 rule or this one usable until July 30, 2024. Residential URL: .../14.007.0006.pdf. No 2024 IECC rulemaking found (CID hearings through 2026-04-21 do not list energy code). Home-rule caveat from the IRC row.

NY.name: New York
NY.scope: Outside NYC (own NYC energy code). Commercial may comply with NYS ASHRAE 90.1 (a NY version of 90.1-2022).
NY.citation: 19 NYCRR Part 1240 (2025 Energy Conservation Construction Code of New York State, Uniform Code)
NY.draft_note: DOS amended notice of adoption (read): 2025 ECCCNYS (pub. July 2025) under 19 NYCRR Part 1240 effective 2025-12-31 with no energy-code transition period (the Uniform Code had an optional 2020/2025 window); permits filed on/after that date must comply. The DOS page does not name the base IECC; DOE state page (2024 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2022, eff 12/31/2025) and ICC product listing say 2024 IECC base. DOS draft rule text (read, PDF) defines 'NYS ASHRAE 90.1' as a NY version of ASHRAE 90.1-2022; the DOS page summary named it 'NYS ASHRAE 90.1-2025' (exact title not confirmed). All-electric provisions (1240.6) suspended by court order. NYC enforces its own NYC Energy Conservation Code. Prior: 2020 ECCCNYS (2018 IECC base).

NC.name: North Carolina

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.scope: Only where a city, county or township elects to enforce the State Building Code; home-rule cities may amend.
ND.citation: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-21.3 (North Dakota State Building Code, 2026 edition), Dept. of Commerce
ND.draft_note: Read the 2026 ND State Building Code Book (Commerce, linked from commerce.nd.gov/community-services/building-codes): 'Effective January 1, 2026, the North Dakota State Building Code consists of the 2024 IBC, IRC, IMC, IFGC, International Energy Conservation Code, and IEBC'; Section 15 holds 2024 IECC amendments; IRC Chapter 11 retained with minor amendments and builders may meet amended IRC Ch. 11 or the amended 2024 IECC. Applies only where a city, county or township elects to enforce the State Building Code (state does not enforce); home-rule cities (e.g., Fargo) may amend. DOE state page still says 'Home Rule' (lag). Prior: 2021 IECC (2022 adoption).

OH.name: Ohio
OH.pending: BBS proposed amendments to the 2019 RCO (notice 2026-07-01), no date; energy changes not confirmed.
OH.scope: Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2019. Residential applies where a certified residential building department exists.

OH.draft_note: Commercial: Cornell LII copy of OAC 4101:1-13-01 (eff 3/1/2024) requires the IECC or ASHRAE 90.1 'listed in Chapter 35'; 4101:1-35-01 (eff 3/1/2024) lists IECC-21 and 90.1-19. codes.ohio.gov shows 4101:1-13-01 amended effective 2025-10-15 (text not shown; assumed same base). Residential: RCO ch. 11 (4101:8-11-01) on the 2018 IRC base (see IRC row), eff 2019-07-01; 4101:8-44-01 lists IECC-18 as referenced standard (chapter eff 4/15/2024). DOE agrees: res 2018 IECC eff 07/01/2019; com 2021 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2019 eff 03/01/2024. Rule text read via Cornell LII, not the codes.ohio.gov PDF.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.scope: Residential is IRC 2024 Ch. 11 as heavily amended by OUBCC; commercial via IBC ch. 13 referencing the 2006 IECC.
OK.citation: OAC 748:20-6-16 (IRC 2024 Ch. 11, amended) and 748:20-2-40 (IBC 2024 ch. 35: IECC-06), 43 Ok Reg No. 20
OK.draft_note: ICC chart lag, not a conflict: chart (Apr 2026) predates the 2026-09-14 rules. Read OUBCC permanent rule PDFs: 748:20-6-16 adopts IRC 2024 Chapter 11 (2024 IECC residential provisions) with heavy modifications (tables replaced, testing only where AHJ requires), eff 2026-09-14. Commercial: OUBCC adopts no IECC directly; 748:20-2-40 (IBC 2024 rule, eff 2026-09-14) changes the IBC ch. 35 IECC reference to 'IECC-06'. The 2006 reference predates this rule (DOE: 2006 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2003 eff 09/14/2022, earlier rule not read), so the 2006 effective date is really earlier. Locals not required to enforce; if they do, OUBCC codes apply. DOE residential still lists 2018 IRC (lag). Commercial IECC 2006 effective date not located: the 2026-09-14 rule only carries it forward (DOE lists 2022-09-14 for the prior rule).

OR.name: Oregon
OR.scope: No IECC: commercial is ASHRAE 90.1-2022 (2025 OEESC); residential is Oregon's own ORSC Chapter 11.
OR.citation: OAR 918-460-0500 (2025 Oregon Energy Efficiency Specialty Code); OAR 918-480 (2026 ORSC Chapter 11)
OR.draft_note: No IECC either side. Commercial: 2025 OEESC based on ASHRAE 90.1-2022 (Sections 1-2 not adopted), effective 2025-01-01, mandatory 2025-07-01 after six-month phase-in; OAR 918-460-0500 amended (BCD adoption release and 25oeesc.pdf cover, via search; Oregon Dept of Energy page agrees). Residential: ORSC Chapter 11 (BCD energy page read: 'Residential energy provisions are located in Chapter 11 of the ORSC'), an Oregon-specific prescriptive/additional-measures chapter, not the IECC (base IECC not named by BCD; Oregon-specific per general knowledge, signer confirm). 2026 ORSC (2024 IRC base) effective 2026-10-01, Ch. 11 mandatory 2027-04-01. DOE agrees: 2023 ORSC res; ASHRAE 90.1-2022 com eff 07/01/2025. Oregon Reach Code is optional.
OR.icc_2026_10_20: ICC chart (Apr 2026): energy columns read 24 and 90.1-2022 (column alignment uncertain)

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.scope: Commercial may also comply with ASHRAE 90.1-2019 (IECC C401.2).
PA.citation: 34 Pa. Code 403.21(a)(9) (IECC 2021) and (a)(7) (IRC 2021 Ch. 11), amended 55 Pa.B. 7701
PA.draft_note: Read 34 Pa. Code 403.21: (a)(9) adopts the 'International Energy Conservation Code of 2021' with PA modifications (residential R401.2.5 excluded, PA U-factor/R-value tables, duct-test exceptions; commercial C105.2.6, C402.5.5); (a)(7) IRC 2021 Ch. 11 similarly amended, some 2018 energy provisions kept. History: amended 2025-11-07, effective 2026-01-01, 55 Pa.B. 7701. Rule text does not mention ASHRAE 90.1 itself; the 90.1-2019 path comes via IECC C401.2 (DOE: 2021 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2019, eff 01/01/2026). Pre-2026 design contracts may use the 2018 UCC during a transition (see IRC row). Prior: 2018 IECC.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.draft_note: RI SOS rule page (read): adopts 'the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC), 2024 edition' with RI amendments, residential (incl. Appendix RK electric-ready) and commercial (incl. Appendix CH); current version effective 2025-12-01; prior version 2022-02-01 to 2025-12-01 (2018 IECC per its purpose text). Page does not mention ASHRAE 90.1 (IECC C401.2 path presumably retained, not confirmed). DOE agrees: 2024 IECC res and 2024 IECC + ASHRAE 90.1-2022 com, eff 12/01/2025. A 3-month prior-code grace to 2026-03-01 is reported for the 2025 code set (search only). Residential IRC (SBC-2) is 2021 but energy follows SBC-8.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.scope: Statute adopts the 2009 IECC unamended except a fireplace rule (6-10-35); commercial may use ASHRAE 90.1-2007 via the IECC.
SC.citation: S.C. Code 6-10-30 (2009 IECC adopted as the Energy Standard), 2012 Act No. 143
SC.draft_note: Read S.C. Code Title 6 Ch. 10: 6-10-30 'The 2009 edition of the International Energy Conservation Code is adopted as the Energy Standard'; history 2012 Act No. 143, effective 2013-01-01 (changed 2006 to 2009); 6-10-35 adds a fireplace damper/combustion-air rule (2013 Act 65). Set by statute, so the 2021/2024 SC building-code cycles do not move it. H.5216 (2026) would limit 6-10-30 to IRC-scope work and let the Codes Council adopt the commercial IECC; passed House 2026-04-29, in Senate Judiciary since 2026-04-30 (likely died at the end of the 2025-26 session; not confirmed). DOE agrees: 2009 IECC and ASHRAE 90.1-2007, eff 01/01/2013.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.scope: No mandatory statewide energy code; 2009 IECC is a voluntary residential standard; cities may adopt their own.
SD.citation: SDCL 11-10-7 (2009 IECC adopted as the voluntary standard for new residential buildings)
SD.draft_note: Read SDCL 11-10-7 via the legislature API: state 'adopts the International Energy Conservation Code of 2009' as 'the voluntary standard' for new residential buildings (SL 2009 ch 63; SL 2011 ch 72). 11-10-8 and 11-10-10 require energy-efficiency disclosure to buyers. No mandatory statewide energy code for residential or commercial; the 11-10-5/-6 IBC design standard (2024 IBC) was not checked for whether its Ch. 13 energy reference binds. Locals may adopt an IECC. DOE agrees: Home Rule, jurisdictional.
SD.icc_2026_10_20: ICC chart (Apr 2026): energy column shows X only (alignment uncertain)

TN.name: Tennessee

(IECC), 2021 edition ... see Appendix for amendments; For one- and two-family dwellings and townhomes, the IECC, 2018 edition ... with amendments'. IECC, 2018 edition ... except that' (2009 testing option/tables substituted); amendments eff 7/16/2020. TX.name: Texas
TX.scope: Residential is IRC Ch. 11 (2015). Cities enforce and may adopt stricter local energy codes.
TX.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code 388.003 (2015 IRC Ch. 11 single-family; IECC commercial), SECO 34 TAC 19.53
TX.draft_note: Read SECO (state adopting agency) pages. Single-family: 'Effective Sept. 1, 2016, SECO adopted the Energy Efficiency Chapter 11 of the 2015 International Residential Code' (history table lists 2009 IRC row as 'Present', an internal inconsistency; text says 2015 is current). Commercial: SECO 'has elected to continue utilizing the IECC (as it existed on May 1, 2015)', effective Nov. 1, 2016, cites 34 TAC 19.53; ASHRAE 90.1 not mentioned on that page. HSC 388.003 read on texas.public.law (secondary; statutes.capitol.texas.gov is a JS app): (a) 2015 IRC energy chapter adopted Sept 1, 2016, SECO may substitute later editions no more than every 6 years; (b) IECC for commercial, SECO may substitute latest edition. SECO adoption page: new process effective Sept 1, 2025, no new edition named. DOE agrees (2015/2015). Enforcement in unincorporated areas not checked.

UT.name: Utah
UT.scope: 1-2 family homes: IRC Ch. 11 replaced by a Utah-written energy chapter (15A-3-203), not IECC-based.
UT.citation: Utah Code 15A-2-103(1)(h) (2024 IECC), amended by 15A-3-701; IRC Ch. 11 replaced by 15A-3-203
UT.draft_note: Read 15A-2-103 (Effective 7/1/2026): '(h) the 2024 edition of the International Energy Conservation Code'; IRC stays 2021. HB 65 (2026 GS) takes effect July 1, 2026 (per the IBC row's read of the enrolled bill). Read 15A-3-203 (Effective 7/1/2026, amended by ch. 47, 2026 GS): 'IRC, Chapter 11, is deleted and replaced with ... Chapter 11, Energy Efficiency (Revised)': fixed R-values (walls R-21, ceilings R-38, U-0.32 windows), REScheck 5% better than 'Utah 2012 REScheck' or HERS 67, duct and envelope testing. That is a state-written chapter, so no residential IECC edition is listed for IRC dwellings. 15A-3-701 amends the 2024 IECC including its R-sections, so IECC 2024 residential provisions likely govern residential buildings outside IRC scope (low-rise multifamily); signer to confirm and decide whether to list a residential 2024 entry. Prior: commercial 2021 IECC (from 2023-07-01); DOE (Sept 2026) lists com 2024 IECC/90.1-2022 eff 2026-07-01 and still res '2021 IECC with amendments' eff 2024-07-01 (DOE lag on the 2026 Ch. 11 rewrite). ICC April 2026 chart (21/21) predates 2026-07-01: chart lag.

VT.name: Vermont
VT.scope: Own codes: RBES (homes <=3 stories) and CBES; 2020 or 2024 editions allowed since 2026-07-14. CBES allows ASHRAE 90.1-2019.
VT.citation: 30 V.S.A. 51 (RBES) and 53 (CBES); Dept. of Public Service RBES/CBES rules adopted 2026-04-10, effective 2026-07-14
VT.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT (residential edition label): PSD update page says the 2020 RBES was 'based on the IECC 2015 with additional language from the IECC 2018 and IECC 2021'; the 2024 RBES rule 'includes changes made to the 2020 RBES'; DOE says res '2018 IECC with amendments'; ICC chart says 21. No single residential IECC edition is listed. Read PSD pages: rules adopted April 10, 2026, effective July 14, 2026, allow compliance with either the 2020 or 2024 RBES/CBES; 2024 RBES/CBES were effective 07/01/2024; 2020 standards effective September 1, 2020. CBES page: 2020 and 2024 CBES are 'standalone documents ... based upon amendments to the IECC 2018 Supplement', with an ASHRAE 90.1-2019 alternative path; CBES covers commercial and residential buildings 4+ stories. Commercial effective date = 2020 CBES (first 2018-based edition, still a permitted path). DOE com '2018 IECC and 90.1-2016' eff 2024-07-01. Rule PDFs themselves not read.

January 18, 2024'. Dwellings use 2021 IRC (N11xx sections referenced). DHCD: 2021 USBC effective Jan. 18, 2024, 2018 USBC optional for one year (per IRC/IBC rows). WV.draft_note: WV SOS register: 87-04 version 8/1/2022 Active; new version In Progress (notice 6/29/2026, agency approved 7/31/2026, LRMRC valid 10/13/2026, modified file 10/14/2026). Read the 10/14/2026 modified-file PDF, which shows current text with strike/insert: 1.4 Effective Date August 1, 2022; '4.1.f ... The 2015 [2024] edition of the IECC for residential buildings' with R402.4.1.2 air leakage max 5 ACH (proposed 3); '4.1.g ... WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.scope: 1-2 family homes: Uniform Dwelling Code SPS 322, Wisconsin's own energy chapter, not IECC-based. Commercial code covers multifamily.
